mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average, particularly when accompanied by a rise in the housing market (HOUST), signals a strengthening consumer demand environment that supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 and HOUST both decline simultaneously in the same quarter, the hypothesis is falsified if S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 3-month moving average, particularly when accompanied by a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market that drives up wages and input costs, reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises while UNRATE falls, the hypothesis is falsified if S&P 500 returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% triggers a tightening monetary policy that raises discount rates, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market that drives up wages and input costs, reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 5% but S&P 500 returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), the hypothesis is falsified.
